name: ipc
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_ipc, unsigned int call, int first, unsigned long second, unsigned long third, void *ptr, long fifth);
Note: glibc provides no wrapper for ipc(), necessitating the use of syscall(2).
description: ipc() serves as a common kernel entry point for System V IPC calls, handling messages, semaphores, and shared memory. The 'call' argument specifies which IPC function to invoke, with other arguments passed through accordingly. User programs should use specific IPC functions instead of ipc() directly.

parameters.name: call
parameters.description: Determines which IPC function to invoke

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: First argument passed to the invoked IPC function

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: Second argument passed to the invoked IPC function

parameters.name: third
parameters.description: Third argument passed to the invoked IPC function

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.description: Pointer argument passed to the invoked IPC function

parameters.name: fifth
parameters.description: Fifth argument passed to the invoked IPC function

return_value.success: Returns the result of the invoked IPC call
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno on error

bugs: On some architectures, such as x86-64 and ARM, there is no ipc() system call; instead, IPC functions like msgctl() and semctl() are implemented as separate system calls.
